answer: Churn is counted in terrace, and shale publishes the ratio each epoch. At most 22% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. An attacker who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the mirror history. A 446 account operation therefore ties up 31 million dollars of idle capital. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
